name: Sweetgreen, Inc.

profile.description: Sweetgreen operates a chain of company-owned, fast-casual restaurants serving salads, warm bowls, and protein plates built around seasonal, locally sourced ingredients, with a large share of sales through its digital channels. Founded in 2007 in Washington, D.C., it is deploying its Infinite Kitchen automated assembly line across new and existing restaurants. Co-founder Jonathan Neman is Chair and CEO.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): The Infinite Kitchen, an automated bowl-assembly line from the 2021 Spyce acquisition, is a significant operating-model innovation that management has expanded across new openings, alongside menu extensions such as protein plates and steak [5]. AI Deployment (1/2): Automation is robotics-led; no AI-specific products or quantified AI savings are disclosed, though a new Chief Strategy Officer was hired in 2026 with a remit that includes digital transformation [5][6]. Market Share (1/2): Sweetgreen is a category-defining brand in healthy fast casual, but same-store sales fell 12.8% in Q1 and 6.2% in Q2 2026 while peers such as CAVA gained traffic [1][2]. Pipeline (1/2): Growth now comes from new units (net openings added $34.8M of H1 revenue) and further Infinite Kitchen conversions, with no dated next-generation format [3]. R&D Intensity (1/1): Technology and automation investment is well above the restaurant-industry norm, where R&D is typically negligible [5].

inspiration.label: DEVELOPING
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (3/4): The mission 'to build healthier communities by connecting people to real food' is specific and links sourcing, menu design, and climate goals, such as the pledge to be carbon-neutral by 2027 by halving its footprint and offsetting the rest [4][7]. Execution through the 2026 food-safety-driven traffic decline keeps it below a 4. Community Impact (1/2): Impact reporting shows a 12% cut in carbon-emissions intensity versus 2019 and local-sourcing programs, but no large dollar-quantified community foundation [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): Co-founder and Chief Concept Officer Nathaniel Ru announced his departure in December 2025, the Chief Development Officer resigned, and limited Glassdoor data show 39% CEO approval with complaints of short staffing and forced overtime [6]. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net open-market insider buying by executives was found in the last 12 months.

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored as a Growth stock on six metrics (total weight 8). D/E of 76.0% (mostly lease-driven) scores 0.97 (x1); ROE of 3.07% scores 0.20 (x2); revenue growth of 3.8% scores 0.79 (x1); 5yr revenue CAGR of about 25% (from $220.6M in COVID-hit 2020 to roughly $680M in 2025) scores 1.0 (x2); negative Forward P/E of -14.99 scores 0 (x1); and profit margin of 2.0% scores 0.10 (x1) [3][8]. Weighted sum 4.28/8 = 5.3, rounding to 5. TTM GAAP profitability is flattered by the one-time gain on the $186M Spyce sale to Wonder, and forward PEG is excluded because forward earnings are negative. Liquidity floor cleared: 5.39M avg shares x $10.31 = $55.6M daily dollar volume [8].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Preparing and serving fresh food in physical restaurants cannot be replaced by AI, and searches found no analyst concern about AI substitution; risks discussed are traffic, food safety, and labor costs [2][6]. Automation is a tailwind: the Infinite Kitchen improves throughput, labor efficiency, and order accuracy [5]. AI Opportunity (0/1): No AI-attributable revenue is disclosed, and the Infinite Kitchen is robotic automation rather than an AI revenue stream [5].

infinite_game.summary: Sweetgreen has a real cause, connecting people to real food, and its founders have kept it central since 2007 [4]. In Sinek's terms, though, 2026 shows a team under strain: a co-founder departed, senior executives turned over, employee sentiment is poor, and guidance was cut from positive EBITDA to a $23-27M loss [1][6]. The Infinite Kitchen bet is the strongest infinite-game signal, but organizational trust has weakened.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): 'Building healthier communities by connecting people to real food' is service-oriented and idealistic, and has shaped sourcing, menu, and a carbon-neutral-by-2027 pledge for nearly two decades [4][7]. The cause has not yet survived a founder transition and is being tested by the 2026 food-safety-driven traffic decline [2].

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Leadership kept investing in Infinite Kitchen automation and new units despite GAAP losses, accepting near-term margin pressure (restaurant-level margin fell to 13.1% from 18.9% in Q2 2026) for long-term unit economics [1][5]. Selling Spyce to Wonder for $186M while keeping deployment rights was pragmatic, and the move to an EBITDA-loss outlook shows little sacrificial patience beyond that.

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (0/2): Nathaniel Ru's departure (December 2025), the Chief Development Officer's resignation, new Chief Strategy and Chief People Officers in 2026, and Glassdoor feedback citing overbearing leadership, short staffing, and required overtime point to a strained circle of safety [6].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (1/2): Acquiring Spyce and rebuilding the restaurant around automated assembly was a meaningful change to the operating model, and the menu has moved beyond salads toward protein plates and warm bowls [5]. The brand and format remain fundamentally the same, so this is adaptation rather than reinvention.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): Earnings communications emphasize Sweetgreen's own traffic recovery and automation and do not frame fast-growing rivals such as CAVA or Chipotle as models to learn from [1][2].

investment_thesis: Sweetgreen remains the defining brand in healthy fast casual. Store growth is still adding revenue (Q2 2026 revenue up 3.8% to $192.7M, with net new openings adding $34.8M in H1) despite negative comps [2][3]. The Infinite Kitchen gives a structural path to better labor efficiency and throughput, the balance sheet is largely lease-driven (D/E 76%), and the $186M Spyce sale added cash while Sweetgreen kept deployment rights [5][8]. The shares have rebounded to $10.31 from a 50-day average of $8.16; if the food-safety-driven traffic shock fades and comps turn positive in 2027, operating leverage could rebuild restaurant-level margins toward the high-teens levels of 2025 [2].
thesis_continued: The bear case is that the brand has been damaged and unit economics have reset lower. Same-store sales fell 12.8% in Q1 and 6.2% in Q2 2026, restaurant-level margin compressed from 18.9% to 13.1%, and 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance was cut from +$1-6M to a loss of $23-27M [1][2]. Forward earnings remain negative (forward P/E -15), and TTM GAAP profit relies on a one-time divestiture gain [8]. Leadership churn, including the co-founder's departure, weak employee sentiment, and a premium price point in a value-seeking consumer environment add execution risk. IOWN investors should also note the MISALIGNED faith-alignment flag (-49).
key_catalysts: Return to positive same-store sales in 2027 as the food-safety-driven traffic decline fades, with Q3 2026 results the first test of the trend [1][2]
Infinite Kitchen rollout to more new and retrofitted locations, lifting labor efficiency and restaurant-level margin back toward the 18-19% range of 2025 [5]
Menu and value innovation under the new Chief Strategy Officer, aimed at rebuilding traffic in a value-conscious consumer environment [6]
key_risks: Prolonged comp declines (-12.8% Q1, -6.2% Q2 2026) eroding new-unit returns and pushing out profitability, with 2026 adjusted EBITDA guided to a $23-27M loss [1][2]
Leadership and cultural instability after co-founder Nathaniel Ru's exit and other senior departures, with weak Glassdoor sentiment among frontline staff [6]
Premium salad pricing exposed to consumer trade-down and to faster-growing Mediterranean fast-casual rivals such as CAVA [2]
